rounding.note: The IESCO tariff guide does not state a rounding rule. Each money component is rounded to the nearest paisa, half up. Products stay exact until that step.

fixed_charge.reason: The IESCO tariff guide shows no fixed charge for lifeline residential consumers.

minimum_charge.reason: The IESCO tariff guide states a minimum monthly customer charge of Rs 75 single-phase and Rs 150 three-phase when no energy is consumed and fixed charges do not apply.

source.issuing_authority: Islamabad Electric Supply Company (IESCO), publishing the schedule under S.R.O. 279(I)/2026
source.reference: A-1 Residential table, lifeline rows, and the minimum-charge note beneath that table
limitations: Rates were read from the IESCO tariff guide on 2026-11-26. The page cites S.R.O. No. 279(I)/2026, February 2026. The day 12 February 2026 is the date K-Electric states for the same SRO at https://ke.com.pk/faqs/. The gazette PDF itself was not retrieved.

The guide lists separate rows named Up to 50 Units (Lifeline) and 01-100 Units (Lifeline). Those labels would overlap if both meant every unit from 1 through 100. They are stored as mutually exclusive bands: above 0 and up to 50, then above 50 and up to 100. The selected band's rate applies to all units.
The guide says lifeline consumers do not receive the benefit of one previous slab. This file uses the single applicable slab method.
This file does not decide whether a household is lifeline. The caller has to confirm that category. Consumption in the current month is not used to classify it.
Consumption above 100 kWh is not given a rate in this file, and the household is not moved to another category.
GST, fuel price adjustment, electricity duty, and TV fee are not in this schedule. Calculated energy or minimum figures are not a payable bill.
No effective end date was published on the page. A later notification is not included in this file.
